Russian Expat Family Style
Feb 2026 • Family
The decor! You come in and it feels like your in a cozy little corner of Moscow. The wallpaper, heavy silverware, drinking glasses, tablecloths. The ambiance reminds you of your great grandmother’s house.

Staff is quite friendly, speaks Russian and Vietnamese (this place was opened by Vietnamese who spent time in Russia). English works here too.

Just what the Doctor ordered.
Jun 2022 • Friends
My good Aussie friend had spent a week in ICU then a week at home resting and was going crazy and needed a pick me up. So I suggested we visit the Russian Restaurant not too far from where we both live in District Binh Thanh in Saigon. Well it was just what the Dr ordered and got him out of the doldrums.
He absolutely loved the food and it turned out when he was young a Russian friend of his mum taught her to make Borscht Soup and so for him it was like comfort food from his childhood days. 
For entree we had what looked like a pasty with lamb in one and pork in the other. We cut them in half so we could experience both without over stuffing ourselves. Next Chris had the Borsch soup followed by the Goulash stew.
I instead went for the Pork Kotleta which looked like a hamburger Pattie but was the texture of soft meatloaf.
Unbelievably tasty. 
We both ordered the potato Dranhiki which is very similar to Scottish Tatties. Very addictive.
Through all of this we shared a jug of their fruit Kompot.
For desserts I chose the Blinchiki and Chris went for the Syrniki.
It turned out his was the better choice of the two desserts available as mine was a little disappointing as it was very dry in the middle and the crepe was too dry also. But the Syrniki was delicious. Chris was very grateful I got him out of his apartment and even reckoned it was the best meal he has had in Saigon so that's saying something.

Superlative by far. An awesome place to dine.
Feb 2022
We lived around the corner, literally a 3-minute walk away from CCCP but never went there. Now that we live 8 km away, we decided to dine here.....ironic.

Better late than never just to find out how good the food is. It's a Friday night and this place was packed, something totally unexpected. But still, the owner found us a place in the corner in under 3-minutes while still smiling and being chatty under all that stress. My compliments!

We were hungry, so the idea was to order as quickly as possible.The first thing my wife set eyes on was the salad, women huh. The Mimosa salad is their signature salad dish, but was sold out (at 730pm???), and the recommendation was to try the Shuba salad. I only know there was some chopped smoked herring located between layers of other chopped veggies, but this tasted so damn good. 

Other dishes ordered included the black Russian caviar, the goulash, russian pork dumplings and to finish off with a Napoleon cake.

My favourite was the salad and the Napoleon cake, but the other dishes were also awesome in their own right. 

Overall, I highly recommend you give this place a chance, and it's almost guaranteed that you'll be making a return trip in short order.

I was surprised how excellent
Jan 2020
I was surprised how excellent the cuisine was at CCCP. 

My wife and I started with the black bread which was soft and tasty. Next we shared the borsch which was unusual. Just a little sour cream and potatoes but with a lot of cabbage. 

The varenhiki (pirogees) were small but very good and a little spicy. The bar be que lamp had a wonderful taste. Finally the cheese filled Chebureki was an excellent way to conclude our meal. 

To drink we had the Kompot. It is made from fruits and is a refreshing beverage. 

Service was efficient. Prices are exceedingly inexpensive.

hanpinn
Singapore, Singapore417 contributions

Can't get enough of Russia but here!
Jul 2018 • Solo
I returned from a vacation in Russia not too long ago and I must say I kinda love Russian food but I know there're dishes that I've not tried before. In Singapore where I come from, there are barely any authentic Russian restaurants around and the gastronomic trend there is not towards Russian food. Hence on my business trip to nearby Vietnam, the thought occurred to me to check out Russian food here since Vietnam has very close ties with Russia compared to many other South East nation countries. 

I'm glad that I went in this direction and was not disappointed. I more or less knew what I wanted to order after trying the real stuff back in Russia and I'm not disappointed. Borsch is as authentic as it gets compared to what I've tasted in Moscow and St Pete's but there's much more fillings in the Borsch. I attempted to try the smoked salted fish "Astrakhan" too but I found it too salty( I haven't tried this when I was in Russia ). Pelmeni was tasty and quite close to what I've eaten in Russia too. Only issue is that it's a little smaller. 

The lady boss can converse well in Russian too( I didn't understand Vietnamese and they didn't have English menus. The next language which I could converse with the locals here was in Russian ) and she explained herself well. Attitude and service was good and the kvass tastes authentic enough. You will see Russian/ Soviet style posters in the shop but the guests which were here were mainly local Vietnamese. Recommended for anyone who wants to try Russian food!
